issues.failure_explanation: The UM-SRD algorithm defined in Section 3 and Algorithm 1 evaluates the explicit finite-volume update on the cut-cell mesh to get $U^* = B(U^n)$ and then sets $U^{n+1} = (1 - s_j) U^* + s_j S_j(U^*)$. Under the stated CFL condition $a\Delta t/h \le 1$ with small cell volume fraction $\alpha < 1/2$, the local CFL number on the cut cell is $a\Delta t/(\alpha h) > 1$. Consequently, $U^*$ is not TVD and generates large spurious over/undershoots. For any monotonic step profile (e.g., $U_i^n = 0$ for $i < j$ and $U_i^n = 1$ for $i \ge j$), the blended update produces $TV(U^{n+1}) > TV(U^n)$ for any $s_j \in [0, 1)$ (for instance, with $\alpha = 0.05, a\Delta t/h = 0.5$, $TV(U^{n+1}) = 19 - \frac{120}{7}s_j$, which is $> 1$ for all $s_j \in [0, 1]$). Moreover, the proof of Theorem 1 does not analyze the UM-SRD operator; it invents an artificial three-step process where blending $R_j(s_j)$ is applied to merged-mesh averages $Q^n$. Because $Q^n$ is already spatially flat on $M_j$, $S_j(Q^n) = Q^n$, making $R_j(s_j)Q^n = Q^n$ identically for all $s_j$. This artificial operator does not match UM-SRD and fails to recover the base scheme $U^*$ when $s_j = 0$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must establish stability of the nonlinear blended update $(1 - s_j^n) U^* + s_j^n S_j(U^*)$ accounting for the state-dependent shut-off mechanism $s_j^n$, or restrict the analysis to the small-cell CFL condition $a\Delta t / (\alpha h) \le 1$ (which would sacrifice the primary advertised objective of cut-cell stabilization).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 1 is completely invalidated. The central theoretical result that UM-SRD is total variation diminishing under the full-mesh CFL condition is false.
issues.title: Theorem 1 claims TVD stability for UM-SRD under full-mesh CFL, but the actual operator is not TVD and the proof analyzes an incompatible merged-mesh scheme
issues.why_classification: Theorem 1 is the primary theoretical guarantee of the paper. Its statement is false as formulated, its proof analyzes an incompatible operator, and any complete resolution requires entirely new nonlinear proof architecture or a major loss in the advertised CFL stability regime.
